title: The influence of green organizational culture on task performance of non-teaching staff of higher educational institutions: Mediating role of contextual performance in Gandaki Province of Nepal
content:
by Nabin Bahadur Adhikari, Bharat Ram Dhungana, Bipin Bahadur Adhikari

Organizational greening is receiving more attention these days. A green organizational culture is essential to saving our ‘home’, the globe, as it promotes environmentally friendly practices across institutions. Because of severe environmental deterioration, not only humans but also day-to-day profit- or non-profit-oriented institutional environments suffer. This study has assessed the relationship between green organizational culture and the task performance of non-teaching staff of higher educational institutions (HEIs) in Gandaki Province, Nepal, and considered contextual performance as a mediating variable. The population consists of TU constituents and affiliated colleges in this region. The independent variable is green organizational culture, which comprises clan, adhocracy, hierarchy, and market cultures, whereas the dependent variable is task performance. Smart PLS 3 was used to analyze the data. Green organizational culture has a significant positive impact on the task performance of non-teaching staff. Contextual performance mediates the relationship between green organizational culture and task performance. The practice of green organizational culture is similar to the public and constitutional campuses. Hence, a green organizational culture is essential for enhancing the task performance of non-teaching staff in HEIs. This research has practical, theoretical, and policy implications and provides insights into the development of various green and sustainable institutions.
author: Nabin Bahadur Adhikari
